title: Truck With a Reserve Tank
statement:
A truck has a main tank holding mainTank litres and a reserve tank holding reserveTank litres. It burns fuel only from the main tank and drives 10 km per litre.

Every time exactly 5 litres have been burned from the main tank since the last check, if the reserve still has at least 1 litre, 1 litre is moved from the reserve into the main tank instantly. The transfer happens in whole 5-litre steps only, never earlier.

Return the total distance in km the truck drives before the main tank is empty.

examples.why: After 5 litres (50 km) one litre moves over. That litre adds 10 km, then the tank is empty.
Transfers happen after litres 5, 10 and 15 burned. The moved litres themselves count toward the next 5, so the truck burns 16 litres, not 13 + 2.
The main tank never reaches 5 burned litres, so the reserve is never used.

hints: Simulate it litre by litre first: burn one, count, and every fifth burned litre check the reserve.
Each transfer takes 5 litres burned but only gives 1 back, so the main tank effectively loses 4 litres per transfer.
Starting from m litres, how many transfers can happen before the tank drops below 5? It is (m − 1) / 4 rounded down, capped by the reserve.

explain.intuition:
Simulate first: burn 5 litres, and if the reserve has fuel, move 1 back. Each round costs the main tank 5 and refunds 1, a net loss of 4. A round can start only while the main tank holds at least 5 litres.

That gives a closed form. With m litres, transfers can keep happening while the tank, after t rounds, still had 5 to burn: m − 4t ≥ 5 before the last round, which allows t = floor((m − 1) / 4) transfers. The reserve may run out first, so take min(floor((m − 1) / 4), reserve). The distance is (m + transfers) × 10.
steps: While the main tank has at least 5 litres: burn 5 (add 50 km), and if the reserve has fuel, move 1 litre over.
Burn whatever is left in the main tank (add 10 km per litre).
Return the distance. Or use the closed form (main + min((main − 1) / 4, reserve)) × 10.
pitfalls: Computing transfers as floor(main / 5). The moved litres also count toward the next 5, as 13, 5 shows.
Moving fuel continuously, for example 0.2 litres per litre burned. The transfer happens only after a full 5 litres.
Forgetting to cap the transfers by the reserve.

complexity.time: O(1) with the formula, O(main) simulated

solutions.title: Simulate in 5-litre rounds
solutions.idea: Burn 5 litres at a time and top up from the reserve when it has fuel, then burn the remainder.

solutions.title: Closed form
solutions.idea: Each transfer costs the main tank a net 4 litres, so at most (main − 1) / 4 transfers happen, capped by the reserve.

followups: The truck moves r litres after every b litres burned. Generalise the closed form.
Why does (main − 1) / 4 rather than main / 4 appear? Check it on main = 4 and main = 5.
